docs.creator: Saul Alinsky
docs.description: First published in 1971, Rules for Radicals is Saul Alinsky's impassioned counsel to young radicals on how to effect constructive social change and know “the difference between being a realistic radical and being a rhetorical one.” Written in the midst of radical political developments whose direction Alinsky was one of the first to question, this volume exhibits his style at its best. Like Thomas Paine before him, Alinsky was able to combine, both in his person and his writing, the intensity of political engagement with an absolute insistence on rational political discourse and adherence to the American democratic tradition.
docs.title: Rules For Radicals

docs.creator: Wartenberg, Thomas E
description: From the Publisher: Using classic films, novels, and plays, Thomas E. Wartenberg explores the central ideas of Existentialism including freedom, authenticity, anxiety, and the Absurd. As well as discussing the ideas of such legendary thinkers as Nietzsche, Camus, and Sartre, Wartenberg shows how Simone de Beauvoir and Franz Fanon use the theories of Existentialism to address gender and colonial oppression. This introduction reveals a vibrant mode of philosophical inquiry that pervades modern culture and addresses concerns at the heart of every human being

Preface -- Introduction -- 1: Existence -- 2: Freedom -- 3: Others -- 4: Anxiety -- 5: Finitude -- 6: Absurd -- 7: Authenticity -- 8: Oppression -- 9: Conclusion -- Further reading -- Bibliography -- Filmography -- Index

docs.creator: Jake Tapper, Alex Thompson
docs.description: Editorial Reviews  Review “A damning, step-by-step account of how the people closest to a stubborn, aging president enabled his quixotic resolve to run for a second term.”  —  The New York Times “ Original Sin  is not really a 'campaign book'—its account of the 2024 election largely ends after Biden drops out—but its simple assessment of the race is more compelling than anything else I’ve read about it . . .  Original Sin  is rarely better than when Tapper and Thompson are writing—with extensive reporting and clear-eyed prose—about the disaster that Biden caused . . . Over the next year, dozens of books will appear that attempt to explain this election. It’s hard to imagine any doing better than that.” — The Washington Post “Explosive . . . Tapper and Thompson have done the [Democratic] party a favor. Some sort of reckoning is due for the disastrous missteps that that paved the way for Trump’s return.”  — Michelle Goldberg,  The New York Times “[The] most significant book to date about Biden’s cognitive decline, which was written by CNN’s Jake Tapper and Axios’s Alex Thompson and draws on hundreds of interviews . . . To their credit, they do little editorializing. The book is written not unlike an autopsy report, describing a gruesome political car crash in dispassionate, clinical detail.”  —The Atlantic “Original Sin is a comprehensively sourced autopsy of the agonised end to Biden’s 50-year career. It’s accusatory, indignant, righteous – and convincing.”  —The New Statesman --This text refers to an alternate  kindle_edition  edition. About the Author Jake Tapper  wrote the bestselling nonfiction book  The Outpost: An Untold Story of American Valor , which was turned into a critically acclaimed film in 2020, and two  New York Times  bestselling novels,  The Hellfire Club and  The Devil May Dance.  He is an Emmy Award-winning TV journalist as lead DC anchor and chief Washington correspondent for CNN. A Dartmouth graduate and Philly native, he lives in Washington, DC, with his wife, daughter, son, three dogs, and cat. Alex Thompson  is a National Political Correspondent for Axios and a CNN contributor. He won the White House Correspondents' Association award for overall excellence in White House coverage for his reporting on Joe Biden in 2024. Before that, he created POLITICO’s “West Wing Playbook” newsletter and worked at  The New York Times  and Vice News. A Harvard graduate, he lives in Washington, DC. He has no pets, but is a proud uncle.
docs.title: Original Sin President Bidens Decline, Its Cover Up, And His Disastrous Choice To Run Again ( Jake Tapper) ( Z Library)

docs.creator: Saul Alinsky
docs.description: Saul Alinsky  (1909 - 1972) • 13 Rules for Radicals • Taktik politischer Kommunikation • 1971 Der Titel "13 Regeln für Radikale" könnte im deutschen Kontext vollkommen missverstanden werden. Der sogenannte "Radikalen-Erlass" hat die politische Semantik leider sogar über Deutschland hinaus nachhaltig verändert und gewandelt.  Traditionell wurde der Begriff der "Radikalität" jedoch früher weder für rechte noch linke Gegner der liberaldemokratischen Republiken gebraucht, sondern im Gegenteil von den linksliberalen Beförderern dieser freiheitlichen Regierungsform als stolze Selbstbezeichnung verwendet.  Noch heute nennt sich zum Beispiel die linksliberale Partei in Dänemark Radikale Venstre  (Radikale Linke), obwohl sie weder mit Kommunismus noch mit Anarchismus irgendetwas im Sinn hat.  Seit 1905 strebt sie eine linksliberale Politik zu Gunsten eines pro-kapitalistischen Wohlfahrtsstaates mit politischen Freiheiten und maximalem Wohlstand für die Mehrheit an. Das Dilemma dieser taktischen Regeln zur politischen Kommunikation besteht seit Donald Trump darin, dass sich mindestens einige von Alinskys Ratschlägen auch für eine in Gänze entgegengesetzte antiliberale Strategie nutzen lassen. Aber das ist das Dilemma, in dem aller Wissenszuwachs und alle Aufklärung stehen. Nicht nur die Freundinnen und Freunde der Freiheit und der Aufklärung werden durch Aufklärung klüger, sondern auch deren Widersacher können aus dem öffentlichen Erkenntnisgewinn für Gegen-Strategien lernen.
docs.title: Saul Alinsky • 13 Rules for Radicals • Taktik politischer Kommunikation • 1971
